validity.recommendation: No change needed. Attach the three verified refs below to the unreferenced value cells (see fills); note the ~3.6% length-measurement variance (87 km vs 84 km) in ResearcherNotes rather than editing the value.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and well documented. Elwatannews (Arabic, 24 Nov 2016) quotes Eng. Ashraf El-Amir, head of Petroshahd company ('the one carrying out operations on behalf of EGPC, ENAP Chile, and Kuwait Energy'), announcing the crude-oil pipeline project: length 87 km, from the company's loading area on the Wahat road, via Qarun Petroleum Company's receiving station, to Dahshour; investment $22 million (line construction + 12 new storage tanks); capacity ~30,000 bpd; intended to move ~19,000 bpd from Petroshahd's fields. Egyptoil-gas.com's feature 'Petroshahd Pipeline: In Simplicity Lies Perfection' (7 May 2017, on-site visit to the East Ras Qattara/ERQ concession, quotes Eng. Sayed Rezk, ENAP Sipetrol GM, and Eng. Gamal Shanhory, Field Manager) independently confirms the pipeline exists, is in service (replaced >100 truck trips/day), is 10 inches in diameter and ~84 km long, running from the Shahd SE field (ERQ's highest-producing field, ~8,000 bpd) to the Petroshahd receiving facility at Qarun Petroleum Company's base on the Wahat road, buried 2 m deep. A third egyptoil-gas.com article ('PetroShahd and PPC to join forces', Dec 2010) independently confirms Petroshahd as 'a joint venture company between EGPC and the Chilean firm Sipetrol' and describes an EARLIER, separate commercial deal to move Petroshahd's crude onward to PPC's Mostorod (Musturad) shipping point -- that onward leg is NOT this 87 km line (Mostorod is a different, much more distant destination than Dahshour) and is not being treated as part of P3692. CLASSIFICATION: correctly an oil (crude) pipeline, not gas/NGL -- both articles explicitly call it a crude-oil transport line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-pipeline Egypt-oil roster; no other row shares this name, these endpoints (El Wahat/Dahshour), or this operator/owner set, so this is not a re-entry of any other PID. ATTRIBUTION: Operator = Petroshahd (Arabic 'بتروشهد') is confirmed by both the 2016 and 2017 articles as the operating entity. Owner1 ENAP Sipetrol + Owner2 EGPC are confirmed by all three articles (Sipetrol described as a subsidiary of Chile's state company ENAP); Owner3 Kuwait Energy is confirmed only by the 2016 elwatannews article (the 2010 article predates Kuwait Energy's stake) -- single-sourced but from the company chairman directly, so plausible and not disputed elsewhere. SPEC: Length 87 km (elwatannews, exact match to GEM's 87.00 km) vs 84 km (egyptoil-gas feature, describing the Shahd SE-to-Qarun leg specifically) -- a ~3.6% variance, well within normal as-built-vs-announced measurement tolerance for the same asset described 6 months apart by different outlets; not treated as a material spec conflict. Diameter 10 in matches GEM exactly (feature article). Capacity 30,000 bpd and Cost $22,000,000 both match GEM exactly (elwatannews). StartYear1 2016 is consistent with the elwatannews announcement date and the feature's 2017 description of the line as already in service. FuelSource 'Shahd SE Field' is confirmed as the pipeline's origin field per the feature article, though the ERQ concession's other fields (Ghard, Rana, Al Zahra, Diaa, Shebl) also produce into the same gathering system via planned/actual tie-ins -- a reasonable simplification, not an error. EndLocation 'Dahshour' (Giza) matches elwatannews exactly; StartLocation 'El Wahat' (Giza) is consistent with both sources' description of the loading/receiving point sitting on the Wahat road. Net: every numeric and attribution field in the sheet is independently corroborated by at least one dated, on-record source, most by two.

fills.researcher_notes: Both the 2016 elwatannews article ('الزيت الخام' / crude oil throughout) and the 2017 egyptoil-gas feature ('Petroshahd Crude Oil Pipeline') describe this explicitly as a crude-oil line.

7 May 2017 on-site feature describes the pipeline as already replacing truck transport ('with their recent application... was able to achieve...'), in service and buried 2 m deep -- an operating asset, consistent with the 2016 announcement plus intervening build-out.
Article dated 24 November 2016 announcing the new pipeline project; single dated source, not independently double-sourced for the exact year, so medium not high.
Petroshahd chairman quoted stating the new line's capacity is 'about 30,000 barrels per day' (نحو 30 ألف برميل يوميا) -- exact match. Single source for this specific figure so medium, not high.

Elwatannews states 87 km exactly, matching GEM. The egyptoil-gas feature (a different outlet, 6 months later) states 84 km for the Shahd SE-to-Qarun leg specifically -- a ~3.6% variance, not an exact independent match, so tier is medium rather than high. Both sources describe the same physical asset; the discrepancy is flagged in ResearcherNotes, not treated as a value error.
'The pipeline is 10 inches in diameter' -- exact match to GEM. Single explicit source, so medium.

Pipeline 'extends from the Shahd SE field, which is the highest producing field with around 8,000b/d.' Note the ERQ concession's other fields (Ghard, Rana, Al Zahra, Diaa, Shebl) also feed the gathering system via tie-ins, so Shahd SE is the named origin/anchor field, not the sole contributor -- fine as recorded, worth a ResearcherNotes caveat.

Elwatannews: line begins at 'the company's loading area on the Wahat road' (بطريق الواحات); the egyptoil-gas feature separately confirms the Qarun/receiving end sits 'on the Wahat road.' 'El Wahat' as recorded is consistent with the Wahat-road corridor named in both sources, though neither gives a discrete named settlement -- medium, not high.
'...ومنها إلى دهشور' (and from there [Qarun's station] to Dahshour) -- exact name match to GEM. Single source names this specific terminus, so medium.
'باستثمارات تبلغ 22 مليون دولار' ($22 million in investment, covering line construction plus 12 new storage tanks) -- exact match. Single source, so medium.

Elwatannews quotes the head of Petroshahd company, described as 'القائمة بالعمليات' (the one carrying out operations) on behalf of EGPC/ENAP/Kuwait Energy. The 2017 egyptoil-gas feature independently corroborates Petroshahd/Enap Sipetrol as the operating entity running the concession and pipeline. Two independent, differently-dated, differently-language sources agree -> high.

Elwatannews (2016) names all three owners exactly: EGPC ('هيئة البترول'), ENAP Chile/Sipetrol ('إيناب التشيلية'), and Kuwait Energy ('كويت إنرجي'). The 2010 egyptoil-gas article independently confirms Petroshahd as a JV between EGPC and Chile's Sipetrol, but predates (or omits) Kuwait Energy. So EGPC+ENAP Sipetrol are two-source confirmed; Kuwait Energy's stake is single-sourced (2016, on the record from the company chairman) -- overall medium, not high, pending a second independent mention of the Kuwait Energy stake.

summary: P3692 Petroshahd Oil Pipeline: existence, classification, attribution and every spec field independently confirmed by dated 2016/2017 Arabic + English press (elwatannews, egyptoil-gas.com); no duplicate on the roster. Verdict confirmed (caveat) -- caveats are a minor 84 km vs 87 km cross-source length variance and Kuwait Energy's ownership stake being single-sourced. 12 refs staged REFS_ADDED, 0 UNRESOLVED.
